techStack.styling: Native CSS with design tokens (CSS custom properties)

findings.title: Zero test coverage — no test framework or test files exist
findings.description: The entire src/ directory contains zero test files (*.test.*, *.spec.*, __tests__/). No testing framework (Vitest, Jest, Testing Library) is installed in devDependencies. A 14-page React SPA with custom hooks, dynamic routing, and interactive components ships with no automated safety net.
findings.impact: Regressions in routing, scroll-reveal hooks, data filtering (blog/events), and form logic go undetected until production. Every deploy to GitHub Pages is a blind push.
findings.recommendation: Add Vitest + @testing-library/react. Start with hook unit tests (useScrollReveal, useDocumentTitle), then component smoke tests for Navbar, ProgramPaths, and critical page renders. Wire `npm test` into the CI pipeline before the build step.

findings.title: CI pipeline skips linting — eslint is configured but never runs in CI
findings.description: The deploy.yml workflow runs `npm ci` then `npm run build` with no `npm run lint` gate. ESLint is properly configured in eslint.config.js with React hooks and refresh plugins, but lint errors never block deployment.
findings.impact: React hooks rule violations, unused imports, and code quality issues can reach production silently. The lint script exists (`eslint .`) but is developer-opt-in only.
findings.recommendation: Add a `lint` step between `Install dependencies` and `Build site` in deploy.yml: `run: npm run lint`. Fail the build on lint errors to enforce the configured rules.

findings.title: Orphaned gh-pages deploy scripts in package.json
findings.description: The `predeploy` and `deploy` scripts (`gh-pages -d dist`) and the `gh-pages` devDependency are legacy artifacts from a pre-GitHub Actions deployment strategy. The active CI pipeline uses actions/deploy-pages@v4, making these dead code that confuses contributors.
findings.impact: Running `npm run deploy` locally would attempt an alternative deployment path that conflicts with the CI pipeline. The `gh-pages` package adds ~12MB to node_modules unnecessarily.
findings.recommendation: Remove `predeploy`, `deploy` scripts from package.json and uninstall the `gh-pages` devDependency. Document the Actions-only deploy model in README.

findings.title: No GitHub environment protection rules for production
findings.description: The deploy job targets `environment: github-pages` but there is no evidence of GitHub environment protection rules (required reviewers, wait timers, branch restrictions). Any push to main deploys immediately.
findings.impact: Accidental or malicious pushes to main go straight to production with no human gate. For a community site with 11K+ followers, an erroneous deploy could affect public-facing content.
findings.recommendation: Configure GitHub environment protection rules for `github-pages`: require at least 1 reviewer for production deploys, or use branch protection rules requiring PR reviews before merge to main.

findings.title: Supabase dependency declared but no environment variables or usage found
findings.description: @supabase/supabase-js (^2.106.1) is listed in dependencies, but no src/ file imports it, no .env or .env.example exists, and no Supabase configuration (URL, anon key) is present. This inflates the bundle and suggests incomplete feature work.
findings.impact: The Supabase client library (~80KB gzipped) ships to every visitor's browser without being used. It also signals planned backend integration (forms, testimonials submission?) that was never completed.
findings.recommendation: If Supabase integration is planned: create .env.example with VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY placeholders, add a src/lib/supabase.js client, and document setup in README. If abandoned: remove the dependency to reduce bundle size.

findings.title: useMultiScrollReveal hook has object-reference instability in dependency array
findings.description: The useMultiScrollReveal hook accepts an `options = {}` parameter, and the useEffect depends on `options.threshold` and `options.rootMargin`. However, each render creates a new options object. While the primitive values are stable, the pattern is fragile — any future non-primitive option would cause infinite re-render loops with IntersectionObserver recreation.
findings.impact: Currently no bug manifests because primitive destructured values remain stable. But the pattern violates React hook best practices and is a latent footgun for future maintenance.
findings.recommendation: Destructure options into primitives at the top of the hook, or use useMemo/useRef for the options object. Same applies to useScrollReveal.

findings.title: No error boundary components for production error handling
findings.description: The React app has no ErrorBoundary component wrapping routes or the root. A runtime error in any page component will unmount the entire app, showing a blank white screen with no user feedback or recovery path.
findings.impact: JavaScript errors from dynamic routes (ProgramDetail, BlogPost with slug params), data parsing, or third-party script failures crash the full SPA. Users see a blank page with no way to recover except manual refresh.
findings.recommendation: Create a top-level ErrorBoundary component wrapping <Routes> in App.jsx. Show a user-friendly fallback with a 'Return Home' link. Log errors to a monitoring service or at minimum to console for debugging.

findings.title: Missing security headers in index.html
findings.description: index.html lacks Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy headers. While GitHub Pages limits server-side header control, meta tags can provide partial protection. The page loads external Google Fonts and has inline scripts.
findings.impact: No CSP means any injected script (via XSS in future user-content features like testimonials) would execute without restriction. The inline 404-redirect script in index.html would be blocked by a strict CSP, so it needs consideration.
findings.recommendation: Add meta CSP tag with at minimum: `default-src 'self'; font-src fonts.gstatic.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' fonts.googleapis.com`. Consider moving the SPA redirect script to a separate file for CSP compatibility.

findings.title: TECHNICAL_DETAILS.md references outdated React version (18 vs actual 19)
findings.description: TECHNICAL_DETAILS.md states 'React 18' in Section 1, but package.json declares react ^19.2.6. The documentation also lists a different workspace path (C:\Users\22036590\Documents\code\website\dzakirah_id) in file links, suggesting it was authored on a different machine and never updated.
findings.impact: Contributors reading the technical docs get incorrect version information. Stale file path links (C:\Users\22036590\...) are non-functional for anyone else.
findings.recommendation: Update TECHNICAL_DETAILS.md to reflect React 19. Replace absolute file paths with relative repository paths. Add a 'last updated' date to the document.

findings.title: Google Fonts loaded without display=swap optimization for critical path
findings.description: Google Fonts are loaded via <link> tags in index.html with `display=swap`, which is good. However, both Lora (7 weights including italic variants) and Outfit (5 weights) are loaded, totaling ~15+ font files. The preconnect hints help, but font loading still blocks first paint on slow connections.
findings.impact: On 3G/slow connections, text rendering is delayed while ~200KB+ of font files download. Indonesian mobile users on limited bandwidth may see layout shifts.
findings.recommendation: Audit which font weights are actually used in CSS and trim unused variants. Consider `font-display: optional` for non-critical weights, or self-hosting fonts to eliminate the external request dependency.

findings.title: No bundle analysis or performance budgeting
findings.description: No rollup-plugin-visualizer, vite-plugin-inspect, or bundle analysis tooling is configured. The Supabase dependency alone adds significant weight. There are no performance budgets defined for bundle size, and no Lighthouse CI in the pipeline.
findings.impact: Bundle size grows unchecked. With Supabase, React 19, React Router 7, and lucide-react, the JS bundle likely exceeds 200KB gzipped without anyone monitoring.
findings.recommendation: Add rollup-plugin-visualizer for periodic bundle audits. Consider vite-plugin-compression for gzip/brotli reporting. Add a Lighthouse CI step in the GitHub Actions workflow.

findings.title: Navbar uses index-based keys for mapped elements
findings.description: In Navbar.jsx, mainNavLinks and mobileNavItems are mapped using `key={i}` (array index) at lines 77, 97, 124, 158. While the nav link arrays are static and won't reorder, this violates React's key best practice. The child items have unique `path` properties that would serve as stable keys.
findings.impact: No immediate bug, but if nav items ever become dynamic (CMS-driven, A/B tested), index keys would cause incorrect DOM reconciliation and lost component state.
findings.recommendation: Use `key={item.path || item.label}` instead of `key={i}` for all nav link mappings. This is a low-risk, high-hygiene improvement.

findings.title: No TypeScript or PropTypes for component contract validation
findings.description: The codebase uses plain JavaScript/JSX with no TypeScript and no PropTypes declarations. Components like ProgramPaths, TestimonialWall, and ProgramDetail accept complex object props (programs, testimonials, event data) with no runtime or compile-time shape validation.
findings.impact: Prop shape mismatches (e.g., a renamed field in programs.js) fail silently at runtime with undefined rendering rather than clear errors. New contributors have no IDE-level guidance on expected prop shapes.
findings.recommendation: Short-term: Add PropTypes to all components accepting complex props. Long-term: Consider gradual TypeScript migration starting with data files (programs.js, articles.js, events.js) to catch shape mismatches at build time.

findings.title: GitHub Actions workflow lacks Node.js version matrix and caching for dist
findings.description: The workflow pins Node.js 20 with npm caching (good), but does not test against multiple Node versions. Since the project uses modern ESM ("type": "module") and React 19, future Node.js LTS upgrades could introduce breaking changes that go undetected until the CI runner updates.
findings.impact: Low immediate risk since GitHub's ubuntu-latest provides a stable Node 20. But when Node 22 LTS becomes default, undetected ESM or API incompatibilities could break builds.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding a matrix strategy testing Node 20 and 22 to catch forward-compatibility issues early. This is optional for a static site but valuable for long-term maintainability.

strengths: Clean GitHub Actions pipeline with latest action versions (checkout@v4, setup-node@v4, deploy-pages@v4)
Proper npm caching and deterministic installs via `npm ci`
Concurrency controls prevent parallel deployment conflicts
Well-structured CSS design system with comprehensive custom properties (60+ design tokens)
SPA routing workaround for GitHub Pages using 404.html redirect pattern
ESLint flat config with React hooks and refresh plugins properly configured
StrictMode enabled in React entry point
Clear separation of concerns: data/, hooks/, components/, pages/ directory structure
Custom hooks for cross-cutting concerns (scroll reveal, document title)
CNAME file in public/ for automatic custom domain configuration
